families.purpose: The Batch API (POST /api/v1/batches). A batch's requests (:in) and its answers (:out), one field per line, each sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from the router's APP_SECRET, the batch id and the hash of the key that sent it, so only that key's batch can read them back. They are kept here, never in the database, so the worker can run the lines and the key can fetch the results.
families.ttl: The sealed requests are deleted when the batch finishes; the sealed answers BATCH_RESULTS_TTL after that (86,400 seconds, 24 hours, unless the operator changed it). A batch that never finishes ends when its 24-hour completion window closes, so nothing outlives the window plus that time.

review.why: A request header kept on purpose so apps can be ranked. It names an application's site, not the caller's network address, and callers can omit it.

columns.name: title
columns.purpose: The X-Title header value, cut to 200 characters: the application's display name.

review.why: A request header kept on purpose for app rankings. It is a short label the caller chooses, not a prompt.

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

tables.name: apps
tables.purpose: Where calls come from, for app rankings: the HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers a caller chose to send, kept as the caller wrote them (truncated). Not recorded for the unlinkable lane.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion: no job or route in the code removes rows from this table.

columns.name: batch_id
columns.purpose: The batch the line belongs to.

columns.name: idx
columns.purpose: The line's position in the batch, from 0.

columns.name: api
columns.purpose: chat or embeddings.

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired.

columns.name: attempts
columns.purpose: How many times the worker started the line (a line whose providers were all unavailable is tried again, up to BATCH_LINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS).

columns.name: status_code
columns.purpose: The HTTP status the line's call returned.

columns.name: generation_id
columns.purpose: The generation the line produced, whose receipt it has.

columns.name: cost
columns.purpose: What the line was charged, after the batch discount, in pico-USD.

columns.name: list_cost
columns.purpose: What the line would have cost without the discount, in pico-USD.

columns.name: failure_code
columns.purpose: For a line that did not succeed, the error type (for example insufficient_credits or batch_cancelled). A fixed code, never text from a request.

columns.name: not_before
columns.purpose: The earliest the line runs (a rate-limited line waits), or, while it runs, when it counts as interrupted.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.purpose: When the line ended.

tables.name: batch_lines
tables.purpose: One row per line of a batch: its status, the HTTP status its call returned, the generation (and so the signed receipt) it produced and what it was charged. No request or answer text: that is sealed outside the database.
tables.retention: Deleted with the batch's sealed answers when its results expire (BATCH_RESULTS_TTL after the batch finished, 24 hours unless the operator changed it).

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: The batch id (batch_ and random hex).

columns.name: account_id
columns.purpose: The account the batch's lines are billed to.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.purpose: The hash of the API key that sent the batch; only that key can read or cancel it.

columns.name: api

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: validating, in_progress, cancelling, completed, failed, expired or cancelled.

columns.name: total
columns.purpose: How many lines the batch has.

columns.name: completed
columns.purpose: How many lines succeeded.

columns.name: failed
columns.purpose: How many lines failed.

columns.name: cost
columns.purpose: What the batch's lines were charged, after the batch discount, in pico-USD.

columns.name: list_cost
columns.purpose: What the same calls would have cost without the batch discount, in pico-USD.

columns.name: discount_bps
columns.purpose: The batch discount in basis points (BATCH_DISCOUNT_BPS when the batch was sent; 5000 is half price).

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

columns.name: started_at
columns.purpose: When the worker started the batch.

columns.name: cancelling_at
columns.purpose: When the key asked to cancel the batch.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.purpose: When the batch's last line ended.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.purpose: The end of the 24-hour completion window: lines not run by then end unrun and unbilled.

columns.name: results_expire_at
columns.purpose: When the batch's answers and line rows are deleted (finished_at plus BATCH_RESULTS_TTL).

columns.name: purged_at
columns.purpose: When they were deleted.

tables.name: batches
tables.purpose: One row per batch sent to the Batch API (POST /api/v1/batches): the key that sent it, its status, how many lines it has and how many succeeded or failed, and what it cost. The requests and answers of its lines are never written to the database: they are kept sealed in Redis or the router's memory (see the Redis section) until the batch's results expire.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion of the row itself; when the batch's results expire (results_expire_at), its line rows and its sealed requests and answers are deleted and purged_at is set.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: Generation id, random. It is also the id of the signed receipt (the X-Receipt-Id response header).

columns.name: ts
columns.purpose: When the call was recorded.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.purpose: SHA-256 of the API key that made the call (the key itself is never stored). Empty for wallet-paid and blind-token calls.

columns.name: account_id
columns.purpose: The account that was billed. For a blind-token call it is the shared token pool, not a person.

columns.name: model_id
columns.purpose: The catalogue model id that answered, such as author/slug.

columns.name: provider_id
columns.purpose: The provider that served the call.

columns.name: tokens_in
columns.purpose: Prompt tokens billed, as a count.

columns.name: tokens_out
columns.purpose: Completion tokens billed, as a count.

columns.name: reasoning_tokens
columns.purpose: Reasoning tokens billed, as a count.

columns.name: cached_tokens
columns.purpose: Prompt tokens the provider served from its cache, as a count.

columns.name: cache_write_tokens
columns.purpose: Prompt tokens written to the provider's cache, as a count.

columns.name: cost
columns.purpose: Total charged to the caller, in pico-USD (1e-12 USD).

columns.name: upstream_cost
columns.purpose: What the provider charged the router for the call, in pico-USD.

columns.name: royalty
columns.purpose: The share of the cost owed to the model's creator, in pico-USD.

columns.name: margin
columns.purpose: The router's fee on the call, in pico-USD.

columns.name: cache_discount
columns.purpose: The discount given for cached prompt tokens, in pico-USD.

columns.name: mode
columns.purpose: How the call was paid: prepaid, per_call, paywith, byok, cache or blind.

columns.name: latency_ms
columns.purpose: Milliseconds until the provider's first response.

columns.name: generation_time_ms
columns.purpose: Milliseconds for the whole call.

columns.name: finish_reason
columns.purpose: Why the model stopped, such as stop or length.

columns.name: native_finish_reason
columns.purpose: The stop reason as the provider reported it.

columns.name: streamed
columns.purpose: Whether the answer was streamed.

columns.name: cancelled
columns.purpose: Whether the caller cancelled before the answer finished.

columns.name: quant
columns.purpose: Quantisation of the endpoint that answered (for example fp8), or unknown.

columns.name: data_region
columns.purpose: The first datacenter region the provider lists, not the caller's location.

columns.name: is_byok
columns.purpose: Whether the caller's own provider key paid for the call.

columns.name: private
columns.purpose: Whether the caller asked for a private route (provider.private or a :private model).

columns.name: attestation_hash
columns.purpose: Hash of the attestation report of the provider, when an attested provider served the call.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.purpose: The receipt's id (the same as id).

columns.name: receipt_sig
columns.purpose: The router's Ed25519 signature over the receipt.

columns.name: receipt_key_id
columns.purpose: Which receipt signing key signed it.

columns.name: receipt
columns.purpose: The signed v1 receipt payload: model, provider, token counts, cost, timing, mode, lane, disclosure class, payer (a key hash or a wallet address), the two SHA-256 digests and a summary of the provider's attestation. Fixed fields chosen by the router.

review.why: Every field is set by the router's receipt code from numbers, ids and hashes; it never copies request or answer text into the payload.

columns.name: receipt_leaf
columns.purpose: This receipt's leaf hash in the anchoring tree.

columns.name: anchor_index
columns.purpose: Which anchor (Merkle root) this receipt was included in, once anchored.

columns.name: leaf_index
columns.purpose: The receipt's position in that anchor tree.

columns.name: receipt_v2
columns.purpose: The v2 receipt claims as JSON: model, provider, lane, hashed request and response, power-of-two token-count buckets and cost units. Null for receipts made before v2.

review.why: Built by buildClaimsV2 from ids, hashes and buckets; the claims carry no payer, address, IP or content.

columns.name: receipt_cose
columns.purpose: The v2 receipt as signed COSE_Sign1 bytes, base64.

columns.name: receipt_leaf_v2
columns.purpose: The v2 receipt's leaf hash in the anchoring tree.

columns.name: leaf_index_v2
columns.purpose: The v2 leaf's position in the anchor tree.

columns.name: paid_with
columns.purpose: For a pay-with call: the token symbol and address, raw units accrued, the fair price used and the swap transaction, when there is one.

review.why: Written by the pay-with code from token symbols, addresses and amounts.

columns.name: payment_tx
columns.purpose: For a per-call payment: the transaction hash that paid.

columns.name: app_id
columns.purpose: Links to the apps row when the caller sent HTTP-Referer or X-Title. Not recorded for the unlinkable lane.

columns.name: attempts
columns.purpose: Every provider the router tried for the call: provider, model, whether it worked, error kind, HTTP status and latency. A failed attempt also keeps up to 200 characters of the provider's own error message, with URLs, keys, emails and long hex removed.

review.why: The failure message is the provider's text, not ours. Providers normally send a generic reason, but a provider could quote part of a rejected request in it, so up to 200 characters of request text could end up here.

columns.name: request_sha256
columns.purpose: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the request body (stream flags excluded). Someone who already has the exact request can check it against this; the text cannot be recovered from it.

review.why: A hash of the request, kept so a receipt can be checked against a request the caller holds; it is 64 hex characters and holds no text.

columns.name: response_sha256
columns.purpose: SHA-256 of the response text (all choices joined). The text cannot be recovered from it.

review.why: A hash of the answer, kept for the receipt; it is 64 hex characters and holds no text.

columns.name: settled_period
columns.purpose: The UTC hour in which the call was settled to the provider, for example 2026-09-26T13.

tables.name: generations
tables.purpose: One row per call the router served: who was billed, which model and provider answered, token counts, cost, timing, how it was paid and the signed receipt. It holds hashes of the request and the response, never their text.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion: no job or route in the code removes rows from this table. Rows are read back for receipts, usage history, settlement and provider scoring.

columns.name: model_id
columns.purpose: The model that was tried.

columns.name: provider_id
columns.purpose: The provider that was tried.

columns.name: ts
columns.purpose: When the attempt finished.

columns.name: ok
columns.purpose: Whether the attempt produced a usable answer.

columns.name: latency_ms
columns.purpose: Milliseconds until the first response.

columns.name: tps
columns.purpose: Output tokens per second, when it could be measured.

columns.name: empty200
columns.purpose: Whether the provider answered 200 with an empty completion.

columns.name: status_code
columns.purpose: The HTTP status the provider returned, when there was one.

columns.name: error_kind
columns.purpose: A fixed code for the failure from the router's ErrorKind list, such as http_5xx, rate_limited, provider_auth, rejected, empty200 or interrupted. Null when the attempt worked.

review.why: One of a short list of codes chosen by the router (ErrorKind); the provider's message is not stored here.

columns.name: source
columns.purpose: traffic for a real call, probe for the router's own health probe.

columns.name: caller
columns.purpose: A 16-character truncation of the SHA-256 of the account id, set only on failed attempts, so one caller cannot single-handedly mark a provider as failing. It is not the account id.

tables.name: health
tables.purpose: One row per provider attempt (and per probe): did it work, how fast, which status. It feeds routing and provider scores. It has no request or answer text and no account id.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion: no job or route in the code removes rows from this table.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: The account id. For a wallet account it is derived from the wallet address.

columns.name: kind
columns.purpose: key for an API-key account, wallet for a wallet account.

columns.name: wallet
columns.purpose: The wallet address of a wallet account. Empty for a key account.

columns.name: balance
columns.purpose: The settled balance: the sum of the account's ledger lines, in pico-USD. A database trigger keeps it equal to that sum.

columns.name: held
columns.purpose: The amount reserved by open holds for calls in flight, in pico-USD.

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

tables.name: accounts
tables.purpose: One row per billing account: an API-key account or a wallet account, with its settled balance and the amount held for calls in flight.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion. The ledger refers to accounts and is append-only, so an account row stays.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: Hold id; for a chat call it is the generation id.

columns.name: account_id
columns.purpose: The account the amount is reserved on.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.purpose: The key hash that made the call, when there is one.

columns.name: amount
columns.purpose: The reserved amount in pico-USD; it cannot change after creation.

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: held, settled or released.

columns.name: kind
columns.purpose: What the hold was for; usage for a call.

columns.name: result
columns.purpose: How the hold ended: the amount charged and any uncovered amount, as strings in pico-USD, and expired: true when the hold timed out.

review.why: Written only by settle() and release() in ledger.ts as { charged, uncovered, expired } amounts.

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.purpose: When an unsettled hold is released automatically (the holds-expire job).

tables.name: holds
tables.purpose: A reservation of balance made before a call runs, settled to the real cost afterwards or released. One hold per call.
tables.retention: The database refuses to delete holds (trigger holds_apply_held), so they are kept permanently.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: Ledger line id.

columns.name: account_id
columns.purpose: The account the line applies to.

columns.name: key_hash
columns.purpose: The key hash the line came from, when there is one.

columns.name: amount
columns.purpose: The signed amount in pico-USD: positive adds to the balance, negative takes from it.

columns.name: kind
columns.purpose: What the line is: deposit, credit, usage, refund, paywith, change, adjustment, withdrawal_lock, withdrawal, blind_purchase and similar.

columns.name: ref
columns.purpose: A unique idempotency reference, such as usage:<generation id> or escrow:<transaction>:<log index>, so a line can never be posted twice.

columns.name: generation_id
columns.purpose: For a usage line, the generation it paid for.

columns.name: description
columns.purpose: A short line written by the router, such as "<model> via <provider>", "USDG deposit <transaction hash>" or "Model usage". Never text from a request.

review.why: Every description is built in code from model ids, provider ids, transaction hashes and fixed phrases (ledger.ts, escrow.ts, indexer.ts); no caller-supplied string is used.

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

tables.name: ledger
tables.purpose: The append-only money ledger: deposits, credits, usage charges, refunds, withdrawals and adjustments. A usage line names the generation it paid for; it does not say what the call was about.

columns.name: id

columns.name: provider_id
columns.purpose: The provider paid.

columns.name: usdg

columns.name: to
columns.purpose: The destination address for the payout.

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: pending, submitted, paid or invoice.

columns.name: tx
columns.purpose: The payment transaction.

columns.name: created_at
columns.purpose: When the row was created.

tables.name: payouts
tables.purpose: A payout to a provider: the amount in USDG, where it went and its status.
tables.retention: No automatic deletion: no job or route in the code removes rows from this table.

columns.name: model_id

columns.name: provider_id

columns.name: tokens

columns.name: requests

columns.name: upstream
columns.purpose: Upstream cost for the hour, in pico-USD.

columns.purpose: SHA-256 of the boot quote the router verified for that host.

columns.purpose: The host's receipt key id.

columns.purpose: The host's raw Ed25519 receipt public key, hex, as its verified quote bound it.

columns.purpose: The Merkle root of the collected leaves.

columns.purpose: Start of the interval the leaves were collected in.

columns.purpose: End of that interval.

columns.purpose: How many leaves the root covers.

columns.purpose: The anchor's index in the on-chain receipt anchor contract once posted.

caveats.text: A request that turns the response cache on has its answer kept, sealed with AES-256-GCM, in Redis and in the router's memory. It is kept for the time-to-live the request asked for in cache.ttl: at most CACHE_TTL_S, which is 3,600 seconds unless the operator changed it, and also the default when the request names none. Requests that do not ask for caching leave nothing here, and a call paid with a blind token, a call on the attested lane or with any disclosure ceiling, a restricted model variant and a streamed answer are never cached. A semantic cache also keeps a 1,024-number hashed word vector of the prompt in memory.
caveats.title: The response cache keeps answers when you ask it to

caveats.text: A batch sent to POST /api/v1/batches has its requests and answers kept, sealed with AES-256-GCM, in Redis (or the router's memory without Redis), never in the database. The sealed requests are deleted when the batch finishes; the sealed answers BATCH_RESULTS_TTL after that (86,400 seconds, 24 hours, unless the operator changed it). A batch that never finishes ends when its 24-hour completion window closes, so nothing outlives the window plus that time. Calls that are not part of a batch leave nothing here.
caveats.title: The Batch API keeps a batch's requests and answers until its results expire

caveats.text: generations.attempts: up to 200 characters of the message a provider sent back when an attempt failed, with URLs, keys, emails and long hex removed. The text is the provider's, not ours; a provider could quote part of a rejected request in it.
caveats.title: A failed provider attempt can keep a short piece of the provider's own error message

caveats.text: apps.url and apps.title: the HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers of a chat call, cut to 500 and 200 characters, so apps can be ranked. Leave the headers out and nothing is kept. They are not recorded on the unlinkable lane.
caveats.title: Two request headers are kept as you wrote them

caveats.text: agent_sessions.metadata, keys.routing, keys.guardrails, keys.tracing, team_audit.detail, preset_versions.config, saved_routes.description, and saved_routes.config hold configuration you write: descriptions, routing and guardrail settings, the system prompts and tool definitions of your presets, session labels. The API checks their shape and size, but it cannot know what you choose to write in a description or a label.
caveats.title: Settings you type are stored as you typed them

facts: Every one of the 56 tables and 659 columns in the database schema is described on this page, and the build fails if a table or column is added without one.

A call leaves a row of counts, cost and timing plus two SHA-256 hashes (request_sha256 and response_sha256) so a receipt can be checked against a request you hold. A hash cannot be turned back into the text.

No table has a column for a network address, and no line the code writes to its log records one. Calls without an API key are rate-limited by the caller's address, which appears only inside a Redis key that expires between 61 seconds and 3,601 seconds after the counting window begins. Over Tor no address is used at all.
summary.headline: We store no prompt or answer text in our database.
summary.reads: This page is about what is kept. It is not a claim that nobody can read a request while it is in flight: on every lane today the router reads the text of a request in memory to route it, and the provider that answers reads it too under its own policy.
